"""Layer 1 MLP down-projection component 5817: the "r + labial" spelling detector.

What it does, in plain terms: this component fires inside words that contain the letter
pair r followed by b, v or w (Latin "rb", "rv", "rw"; Cyrillic "р" followed by "б" or "в").
Those pairs are the spelling of serv-, observ-, conserv-, preserv-, herb-, Serb-, verb-,
Berber-, and so on. Its activation is largest on a short word fragment (no leading space,
at most 5 letters) that completes such a pair with its b/v/w letter: "ERV" in
OBSERVATION, "v" in Arvind, "w" in konserwacja, Cyrillic "в" in резерв. Capitalised
fragments such as "ERV" fire about twice as strongly. Smaller
values come from the other fragments of such words, and whole English words that
happen to contain the pair (service, forward, board) stay near zero.

The program tracks the letters of the current word (reset at any non-letter and at a
new document) and reads only the newest token.
"""

import re

READS = ()

# r followed by b, v or w; Cyrillic р followed by б or в
CLUSTER = re.compile(r"r[bvw]|р[бв]")
LABIAL = "bvwбв"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    word_before = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else ""
    # the letters of the current word, through this token
    word = word_before + token
    tail = len(word)
    while tail > 0 and word[tail - 1].isalpha():
        tail -= 1
    word = word[tail:].lower()

    in_cluster = CLUSTER.search(word) is not None
    was_in_cluster = CLUSTER.search(word_before.lower()) is not None
    if not in_cluster:
        return (doc, word), 0.0

    core = token.strip()
    short_fragment = core.isalpha() and len(core) <= 5 and not token.startswith(" ")
    completes_here = in_cluster and not was_in_cluster
    has_labial = any(c in LABIAL for c in token.lower())
    value = 0.3 + (0.2 if short_fragment else 0.0)
    if short_fragment and has_labial and completes_here:
        capitals = core.isupper() and len(core) > 1
        value += 2.6 if capitals else 1.3
    return (doc, word), float(value)

What it does, in plain terms
- Mostly quiet. Across all text its activation is small (typically within +-0.1) and
  noisy; this program predicts 0 for nearly every token.
- Name fragments after "sh": when a word is split into pieces and its first piece is a
  bare "Sh" or "sh" (Sh|illing, Sh|eng, Sh|ang, Sh|um|ard), the next piece, if it is a
  lowercase Latin fragment, gets about +0.6 (the real values run from about 0 to +9).

  negative (about -3 to -8); 座 (course/seat), 注册 (register) and 册 (booklet) are

  because early positions in a document have the largest activations.

Token identity alone (a lookup table) explains about 15% of the variance on held-out text,
but that comes from thousands of rare tokens; these few rules explain about 5-7%.

CHINESE_WORDS = {
    "坛": -4.0,  # arena, as in 政坛, 文坛, 体坛, and on its own
    "论坛": -3.0,  # forum
    "座": -1.0,  # seat, course (讲座)
    "注册": -1.0,  # register
    "册": -1.5,  # booklet, volume
    "冊": -1.5,  # traditional form of 册

    t = prefix.position

    word = token.strip()

    previous = prefix.token_strings[t - 1].strip().lower()

'library name after lib' and 'from ... onward' signals into the residual stream.

What it does, in plain terms (all rules look only at the current token and a few
tokens before it):

   attached lowercase name (lib|usb, lib|crypto, lib|curl, lib|xml, /lib|cuda)

   libusb, libcurl, libcrypto, libxml. The same rule also fires on the rare
   non-software words that start with "lib" (librería, libro, liberal), where the
   true activation is near zero: a known false-positive source.

   "from __future__") is strongly negative (about -5). Generic particles
   (on, an, up, down, until, aus) get a mild -1 only when "from" is within three
   tokens before them.

   that no short rule captures.

FROM_WORDS = {"from", "von", "ab", "since", "从", "自", "從", "自从", "hence"}
GENERIC = {"on", "an", "up", "down", "aus", "until", "upon"}
STRONG = {"onward", "onwards", "forward", "forwards", "forth", "upward", "upwards",

        return None, 2.2
    if (cur in STRONG or raw.endswith(CHINESE_START)) and any(x in FROM_WORDS for x in window):
        return None, -5.0
    if cur == "future" and prev.strip() == "__" and "from" in window:
        return None, -5.8
    if cur in GENERIC and any(x in FROM_WORDS for x in window[-3:]):

"""Layer 1, MLP hidden unit 5822 (down_proj component 5822), explained as a sparse text detector.

Almost every position sits near zero. The large values come from a few recognisable
kinds of text, so the program predicts those and otherwise predicts 0.

1. OEIS pages (the On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences). Once a marker of such a
   page ("OEIS", "OFFSET", "internal format)", "Integer Sequences") has appeared in the

   CROSSREFS, EXAMPLE, FORMULA, refs, list, graph, Greetings, and the "n" in
   "Table of n, a(n)". Typical value about -1.7, up to -10 on the "S" of LINKS.
2. A named JavaScript import: the "{" right after "import" goes strongly positive
   (about +1.7), and the "{" after "const" weakly (+0.6).
3. A run of middle dots (a dot leader, "····") is about +0.5.
4. The first token of each document is slightly positive (+0.2). At a document's start
   attention can see only that token, so the value depends on the token alone.

Everything else predicts 0. Values are the least-squares fit of these indicators to the
component's activations on training text.

import re

READS = ()

OEIS_MARKERS = ("OEIS", "OFFSET", "internal format)", "Integer Sequences")
OEIS_LABEL = re.compile(r"\s?[A-Z]+|\s?n|\(n|\(")
DOT_RUN = "·"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    text, seen = carry if carry else ("", False)
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    first = len(docs) == 1 or docs[-1] != docs[-2]
    if first:
        text, seen = "", False
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    before = "" if first else prefix.token_strings[-2].strip()
    text = (text + token)[-200:]
    seen = seen or any(marker in text for marker in OEIS_MARKERS)

        value = 0.2

        value = 0.5
    elif token == " {" and before == "import":
        value = 1.7
    elif token == " {" and before == "const":
        value = 0.6
    elif seen and OEIS_LABEL.fullmatch(token):
        value = -1.7
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return (text, seen), value

"""Approximate a spelling feature centered on vowel + i.

Marked Vietnamese i-final vowel groups are positive. Their strength depends on
accent marks and whether the syllable is a very frequent word. The words
với (with) and đối (opposition) are especially strong.
A split-off i is positive after o and in Vietnamese-looking context; Hungarian
and Romanian suffix contexts can make it negative. Repeated middle dots are
negative. These are approximate spelling rules, not a phonetic analysis.
"""
from functools import lru_cache
import unicodedata
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency

READS = ()


def plain(text):
    return ''.join(c for c in unicodedata.normalize('NFD', text.lower())
                   if not unicodedata.combining(c))


@lru_cache(maxsize=16000)
def marked_vowel_i(text):
    word = text.strip().lower()
    if len(word) < 2 or not word.endswith('i'):
        return None
    vowel = unicodedata.normalize('NFD', word[-2])
    if vowel[0] not in 'aeou' or len(vowel) < 2:
        return None
    marks = unicodedata.normalize('NFD', word)
    frequency = zipf_frequency(word, 'vi')
    if '\u0301' in marks:                  # acute tone
        if '\u0302' in marks:              # circumflex vowel, usually ôi
            return 4.57 if word == 'đối' else 2.39
        return 3.36 if word == 'với' else 0.66
    if frequency > 6.42:
        return 0.19
    return 1.73 if frequency <= 4.77 else 0.76


@lru_cache(maxsize=100000)
def token_kind(text):
    word = plain(text.strip())
    single_i = text in ('i', 'I')
    continuation = (not text[:1].isspace() and text.lower().startswith('i')
                    and len(word) <= 3
                    and (len(word) == 1 or word[1] not in 'aeiou'))
    digraph = (not text[:1].isspace() and len(word) <= 6
               and word.endswith(('ai', 'ei', 'oi', 'ui')))
    return word, single_i, continuation, digraph


def vietnamese_context(text):
    # Horned vowels / barred d, or the hook and dot-below tone marks.
    return (any(c in text for c in 'ơưđ') or
            any(c in unicodedata.normalize('NFD', text)
                for c in '\u0309\u0323'))


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    context = '' if carry is None or carry[0] != doc else carry[1]
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    new_carry = (doc, (context + text.lower())[-200:])
    value = marked_vowel_i(text)
    if value is not None:
        # Bare acute/grave vowels also occur in pinyin and other languages.
        word = plain(text.strip())
        marks = unicodedata.normalize('NFD', text.strip())
        ambiguous = (all(c in 'aeiou' for c in word) and
                     not any(c in marks for c in '\u0302\u031b\u0309\u0323'))
        if ambiguous and not vietnamese_context(context):
            value = 0.0
        return new_carry, float(value)
    if text == '··':
        return new_carry, -2.45 if context.endswith('·') else 0.0
    word, single_i, continuation, digraph = token_kind(text)
    if not (single_i or continuation or digraph):
        return new_carry, 0.0
    last = plain(context[-1:])
    vowel = bool(last) and last in 'aeiouy'
    continuation = continuation and bool(context)
    hungarian = (bool(set(context) & set('őű')) or
                 sum(w in context for w in
                     (' az ', ' és ', ' hogy ', ' egy ', ' nem ')) >= 2)
    vietnamese = vietnamese_context(context)
    romanian = (bool(set(context) & set('șțşţîă')) and
                any(w in context for w in (' de ', ' din ', ' cu ')))
    value = 0.0
    if single_i:
        value = {'a': -0.18, 'e': -0.10, 'i': -0.20,
                 'o': 0.59, 'u': 0.20, 'y': -0.18}.get(last, 0.0)
        if romanian:
            value -= {'i': 0.79, 'e': 0.47}.get(last, 0.0)
        if hungarian and not vowel:
            value -= 0.35
        if vietnamese and not vowel:
            value += 0.36
    elif continuation and vowel:
        value = 0.03
    if continuation and vowel:
        if vietnamese:
            value += 1.89
        if hungarian:
            value -= {'a': 2.34, 'e': 0.88, 'o': 1.78}.get(last, 0.46)
    if digraph and not continuation:
        value += 0.54 * (word == 'oi')
        value += 1.14 * vietnamese - 2.88 * hungarian
    return new_carry, float(value)

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:5823 -- a Vietnamese "-oi" word detector, plus a document-start dip.

What it does, in plain terms:
  * It fires on Vietnamese words whose spelling ends in the vowel pair "-oi" (with its
    diacritics: ố, ới, ôi, ơi, ổi, ồi, ...), and more weakly on Vietnamese words ending in
    "-ai". The strongest are the common words đối, với, thời, mối, nối, lời, giới, gợi,
    môi, khởi, nội (about +2 to +5). A few "-ai" words (giải, cái, loại, ngoài, đại) give
    about +1.5 to +3. Words typed without diacritics ("doi", "voi", "moi") fire weakly
    (about +0.4), except "soi" (as in "soi cầu"), which fires strongly.
  * The word is the letters typed so far in the current word, so a word split over two
    tokens (for example "so" + "i" = "soi") counts as one word.
  * The first token of every document (the start of a packed row, or after a document
    boundary) gets a small negative value (about -0.33), since its activation there is
    usually negative.
  * Everything else is 0.

Why: the component's large activations are almost all on these Vietnamese -oi/-ai syllables;
its other activity is small noise that a short program cannot predict.
"""

import unicodedata

READS = ()

# Vowels with diacritics, used only to tell Vietnamese spelling from plain ASCII.
MARKS = set("ăâđêôơưàáảãạằắẳẵặầấẩẫậèéẻẽẹềếểễệìíỉĩịòóỏõọồốổỗộờớởỡợùúủũụừứửữựỳýỷỹỵ")

# Words (diacritics stripped) ending in -oi, with the typical activation for each.
OI_WORDS = {"doi": 4.7, "voi": 3.4, "phoi": 3.2, "thoi": 2.7, "moi": 2.6, "noi": 2.4,
            "khoi": 2.4, "gioi": 2.2, "loi": 2.2, "goi": 2.2, "duoi": 1.7, "soi": 2.7}
# Words (diacritics stripped) ending in -ai, with the typical activation for each.
AI_WORDS = {"giai": 2.8, "cai": 2.4, "loai": 1.7, "ngoai": 1.6, "dai": 1.4}

DOC_START = -0.33


def _strip_marks(text):
    """Lower-case text with diacritics removed, e.g. 'đối' -> 'doi'."""
    return "".join(c for c in unicodedata.normalize("NFD", text.lower())
                   if unicodedata.category(c) != "Mn")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    new_doc = prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if new_doc:
        word, marked = "", False
    else:
        word, marked = carry

    # Extend the current word with this token's letters; punctuation or spaces start a new word.
    piece = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    breaks = [i for i, c in enumerate(piece) if not c.isalpha()]
    if breaks:
        word, marked = "", False
        piece = piece[breaks[-1] + 1:]
    word += _strip_marks(piece)
    marked = marked or any(c in MARKS for c in piece.lower())
    carry = (word, marked)

    if new_doc:
        return carry, DOC_START
    if word in OI_WORDS and (marked or word == "soi"):
        return carry, OI_WORDS[word]
    if marked and word in AI_WORDS:
        return carry, AI_WORDS[word]
    if word.endswith("oi"):
        return carry, 1.0 if marked else 0.4
    return carry, 0.0
